build.title: Hotfix: toolbar settings still change nothing (live console)

said.text: Brett (Nov 14): 'the toolbar settings still don't work. When I click the toolbar and go to its settings, the settings don't change anything.' Earlier builds touched this (fix-toolbar-settings-doing-nothing, chrome-settings-actually-apply-toolbars, per-toolbar-settings PR #650, per-instance picker #642/#622) but it's still broken on the live console. Reproduce on the LIVE console first (open a toolbar's settings, change each setting, confirm whether the stored value changes and whether the toolbar re-renders). Find which of those PRs never landed vs. what's genuinely broken, land or fix, and verify on the live console after redeploy.

# Build: hotfix-toolbar-settings-still-change

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Hotfix: toolbar settings still change nothing (live console)" (hotfix-toolbar-settings-still-change) [hotfix] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (4 left, ~1.2 h):
[ ] s1 (~15 min) Reproduce on the live console: open a toolbar's settings, change each one, log whether the value saves and whether the toolbar redraws
[ ] s2 (~15 min) Check which earlier toolbar-settings PRs (#650, #642, #622, chrome-settings-actually-apply-toolbars) landed; find the real break
[ ] s3 (~25 min) Fix so every toolbar setting applies live to that toolbar; add a test that changes each setting and checks the toolbar changed
[ ] s4 (~15 min) Land through the queue, confirm on the live console after redeploy, phone alert to Brett when verified
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step hotfix-toolbar-settings-still-change <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link hotfix-toolbar-settings-still-change --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step hotfix-toolbar-settings-still-change <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note hotfix-toolbar-settings-still-change "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.
